creature.name: Deathless Zealot of Zagresh

mid.name: Field of Slaughter
entries: 40 feet. Allies within the aura treat their weapons and unarmed attacks as keen, even if the weapons don't meet the requirements. Critical hits within the aura deal 3d6 persistent bleed damage, in addition to any other critical hit effects. If the critical hit would already deal persistent bleed damage, increase the damage to 3d6+3.

mid.name: Ravage Heretic
mid.trigger: A creature within 60 feet who the deathless zealot can see and who doesn't worship Zagresh casts a divine spell
entries: The deathless zealot attempts to counteract the triggering spell using their spell attack modifier and a counteract rank of 5. If the spell is counteracted, the caster is stunned 3 from the pain of the backlash. If the deathless zealot fails to counteract the spell, the caster is temporarily immune to further uses of this ability for 24 hours.

mid.name: Spellsmash
entries: The zealot Casts a Spell that requires a spell attack roll or has a range of touch, channeling it into their greatclub, then makes a melee Strike. This attack roll determines the effects of both the Strike and the spell. This counts as two attacks for their multiple attack penalty, but the penalty isn't applied until after the Spellsmash. The zealot can't use Spellsmash again until they recharge it with a single action, which has the concentrate trait.

_aon.markdown:
Ancient dwarves paid little attention to the Sea of Dirt, seeing little worth harvesting from its muck. Orcs were considerably braver, yet even they're wary of monsters swimming through the silt. To an outsider, palpares might seem like a cautionary tale to keep children from sinking into the quicksand, and the large pits found dotting the Sea of Dirt's shores are just geological phenomena that appear in the wet season. Those who have stumbled across these traps know the dangerous reality. Few know much about palpares, an enormous insect whose plated, hulking abdomen takes up most of its size. They seem to be solitary ambush hunters that hibernate during the dry season, then awaken during the Flood to create their enormous pit traps. These traps capture prey of all sizes, even the occasional herd of migrating aurochs, as they wait buried in the center. Though usually very patient, when disturbed, a palpares can move through its native sandy soil surprisingly quick, greeting intruders who enter its domain with its shovellike head and vicious pincers. **[Recall Knowledge - Animal](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 30 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 28 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 25 [Palpares](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3768) **Source** [Pathfinder #209: Destroyer's Doom](/Sources.aspx?ID=251) pg. 85 **Perception** +19; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=82) ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 90 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +23, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +26, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +22, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +19 **Str** +8 **Dex** +7 **Con** +5 **Int** -4 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +2 --- **AC** 31 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +24 **Will** +18 **HP** 195 **Dig In** **Trigger** The palpares is aboveground and would take damage; **Effect** The palpares [Burrows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) up to its Speed, throwing up a shield of dirt that reduces the damage by 11. --- **Speed** 25 feet, burrow 35 feet **Melee** pincers +24 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 2d8+10 piercing plus [Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=45) and palpares venom **Melee** body +24 ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 2d8+12 bludgeoning **Breaching Ambush** **Requirements** The palpares is underground; **Effect** The palpares [Burrows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) up to twice its Speed underneath a creature, then Strikes upward with its pincers, ending aboveground. **Palpares Venom** ([Incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [Poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) **Saving Throw** DC 30 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 3d6 poison damage and [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) (1 round); **Stage 2** 3d8 poison damage and stunned 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 3d10 poison damage and [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85) (1 minute) **Pit Trap** The palpares [Burrows](/Actions.aspx?ID=2310) to create a 30-foot radius sloping pit centered on itself that's 10 feet deep at the center. All creatures in the area must attempt a DC 30 Reflex save.
**Critical Success** The creature is [moved](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) by tremors to a square outside the edge of the pit.
**Success** As critical success, but the creature is also [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature falls 10 feet into the pit and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).
**Critical Failure** As failure, and the creature is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93). **Venomous Bite** **Requirements** The palpares has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77); **Effect** The palpares uses its mandibles to inject venom, dealing 3d8 acid damage and exposes the creature to palpares venom.
Life Stages Research suggests palpares aren't yet in its final form of life, as large caverns on the shores have been discovered to hold traces of chitin and the rotting remains of palpares partially transformed. Though nobody has encountered an adult and lived to tell the tale, rumors abound that the fully fledged insect form resembles [Rovagug](/Deities.aspx?ID=291). Communities are quick to locate and dispose of any pupae they find in large, sand-encrusted mounds in the dirt. Some towns hold large barbecues to harvest tons of “mud bacon.”

**Pounce** <actions string="Single Action" />  The warcat of Rull Strides and makes a Strike at the end of that movement. If the warcat began this action [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), it remains hidden until after the attack.

**[Rend](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=73)** <actions string="Single Action" />  claw

</column>

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="/images/Icons/Sidebar_4_RelatedCreatures.png">Apex Predator</title>

The warcat of Rull is a stealthy predator that roams a large territory, hunting alone or with a mate. Even when nursing cubs, warcats hunt for themselves and teach their cubs to be self-sufficient. Warcats fear no challenge, preying on megafauna, giants, and even young dragons.
</aside>

mid.name: Experienced Tracker
entries: An orc hunter can Track while moving at full Speed.

mid.name: Hunt Prey
entries: The orc hunter designates a single creature as their prey. They must be able to see or hear the prey, or must be tracking the prey during exploration. They gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to Seek their prey and a +2 circumstance bonus to Survival checks to Track their prey. They also ignore the penalty for making ranged attacks within their second range increment against the prey. They can only have one creature designated as their prey at a time. If they use Hunt Prey against another creature, the prior creature loses the designation and the new prey gains the designation.

mid.name: Hunter's Edge
entries: The orc hunter deals an additional 1d8 precision damage the first time they hit their hunted prey in a round.

<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="/images/Icons/Sidebar_2_AdditionalLore.png">Hunting Trophies</title>

Orc hunters frequently take bone fragments from megafauna or powerful opponents they slay as trophies.
